clue.text: Appear much pained, having to share room

definitions.meaning: to bend over double in agony, as with a stomach cramp
to sleep two to a room or bed when space is short

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both bending over in pain and two people bunking together in one space.

clue.text: Angled, addressing fish out loud?

indicators.note: the question mark and 'out loud' tell us the phrase is to be heard, not read

parts.note: O is the vocative used when addressing someone, and a bleak is a small river fish: 'O bleak!'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether talking to a fish counts as speaking at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out loud' signals that O BLEAK, a call addressed to the fish, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slanting, at neither a right angle nor parallel, is described by this word.

clue.text: Officer seen briefly in square rigger

definitions.text: Officer seen briefly in square rigger

parts.words: Officer seen briefly in square rigger
parts.note: the shortened written form of this army rank is BRIG, which is also a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship

explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen briefly' means the abbreviation: the rank's short form spells a type of square-rigged ship.
explanation.definitionFit: This army rank sits above a colonel and commands a brigade.

clue.text: One's late leaving

parts.note: 'late' here means dead, so this is what a deceased person leaves behind to heirs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone departing late; 'late' actually means deceased, and the 'leaving' is a bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's property and possessions passed on at death are known by this legal term.

clue.text: Plain glass used in pioneering vehicle

parts.note: a prairie is a wide grassy plain of North America
a schooner is a tall drinking glass, used for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: Plain glass was put to use in some early, groundbreaking vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The covered wagon of American settlers heading west was nicknamed for its sail-like canvas.

clue.text: Stage is hardly the environment for this Oriental entertainer

indicators.note: the surrounding words form the setting that encloses the wanted run of letters

explanation.surface: A theatre stage is said to be a poor setting for a certain Japanese hostess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The environment for' says the answer sits inside 'Stage is hardly'; 'this' simply points from the surface to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese hostess trained in music, dance and conversation is this kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Succeeded in continuing rum business

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the middle of the phrase for continuing

parts.note: going on means continuing
s. is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone has managed to keep going in an odd line of trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' is British for odd or strange, so 'rum business' is strange happenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange or suspicious happenings are described with this informal phrase.

clue.text: Expose no member of the monarchy

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to lay open to something, as in exposing someone to danger
a citizen ruled by a monarch, not one of the royals

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to lay open to; as a noun it is a person owing allegiance to a sovereign.

clue.text: Tsarina's London palace

definitions.meaning: the wife of Nicholas II, last Tsar of Russia, had this name; the 's reads as 'is'
a large Victorian entertainment venue in north London, known as Ally Pally

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is': the last Tsarina was this, and so is a north London palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The last Russian empress bore this name, as does a famous palace in north London.

clue.text: Exhibition of rue — perhaps a shrub one's into

indicators.note: the numeral for one goes into the word for vegetation

parts.note: a shrub is an example of a plant
I is the Roman numeral one; 'one's into' means one is into

explanation.surface: A display of the herb rue, with some shrub planted among it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rue is both a herb and regret; the plant sense leads the solver astray from the definition, which means a show of sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament or complaint is a display of sorrowful regret.

clue.text: Friendly before cold reception, and after

definitions.text: Friendly before cold reception, and after

indicators.note: the word receives the cold letter, taking it inside

parts.note: amiable means friendly
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is warm until given a chilly welcome, and still warm afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: AMIABLE means friendly before it takes in C; after the reception, the resulting word is still friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well disposed and courteous, as in a cordial settlement, is what this word describes.

clue.text: Temporary lodger is comparatively dumpy

definitions.meaning: someone occupying an empty building without right or rent
more short and thick, the comparative of the adjective

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an unlawful occupant of a property; the other is the comparative of an adjective for short and stout.

clue.text: Animal classifications not entirely standard

indicators.note: the synonym for standard loses its final letter, so it is not complete

parts.note: general means usual or standard, as in general practice

explanation.surface: Ways of grouping animals that are not wholly conventional.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, groups ranked between family and species are the plural of genus.

clue.text: Bird — it sat on bench

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece sitting on another comes after it

parts.note: a pew is a bench in a church

explanation.surface: A bird perches on a bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the lapwing, a plover with a call imitated by its name.

clue.text: Ceremony requiring a severe hairstyle

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
dour means stern or severe

explanation.surface: A formal occasion calls for a strict hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A style with hair swept up high from the forehead, named after Louis XV's mistress.

clue.text: Given award for architectural style

definitions.meaning: the middle phase of English Gothic architecture, around the 14th century

explanation.definitionFit: Honoured with a medal is one sense; the other is the ornate second period of English Gothic building.

clue.text: Close shaves for pilots making appearance with young ladies

parts.note: an air is a manner or appearance
misses are young unmarried women

explanation.surface: Pilots have near disasters while showing off to young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Near collisions between aircraft are this former term for near misses.

clue.text: Between plump and lean, a person expecting no choice

indicators.note: the single letter sits between the two synonyms

parts.note: fat means plump
list means lean, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Caught between being stout and thin, someone resigns themselves to no choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' is not thin here but the verb for a ship tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes events are predetermined and cannot be changed.

clue.text: Formidable woman's never-ending ordeal in American literary family

indicators.note: the shortened ordeal goes in the family name

parts.note: the March sisters are the family of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women

indicators.note: the synonym for ordeal loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is an ordeal

explanation.surface: A formidable woman suffers endless trials within a famous American family of novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never-ending' cuts TRIAL to TRIA, which goes 'in' MARCH; the 's reads as 'is' or 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who heads a family or group, often a commanding figure.

clue.text: Plane's maximum height, say

parts.note: the plane is not an aircraft but a plane tree, whose highest point is meant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft's ceiling; it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of a tree such as a plane.

clue.text: Girl turned over a shiny fabric

indicators.note: the whole phrase is read backwards

parts.note: cire is a fabric with a glazed shiny surface

explanation.surface: A girl flips over a glossy cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' reverses A CIRE as a whole, giving the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name.

clue.text: Forced firm creed to be revised

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the creed is to be rewritten, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm's creed is forcibly revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as an adjective qualifying the creed, but it is the noun, a company; 'to be revised' gives ERCED.
explanation.definitionFit: Compelled by pressure or threats.

clue.text: Host, for example, interrupts celebrity

indicators.note: the abbreviation breaks into the word for a celebrity

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity, as in literary lion

explanation.surface: A party host breaks into a famous guest's conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a party-giver but means a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host in the sense of a vast number or army.

clue.text: This paper's contents could result in action

definitions.text: This paper's contents could result in action

parts.words: This paper's contents could result in action
parts.note: a list of business for a meeting, from the Latin for things to be done

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a legal threat; it is a meeting's list of items to act upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be discussed at a meeting.

clue.text: Partisan is, indeed, so revolutionary

indicators.note: the letters are turned around in a revolution, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A biased person is, indeed, so very radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' rearranges INDEED SO; 'is' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Biased towards one party's view.

clue.text: Clearly, I'll see if he can help me

definitions.text: Clearly, I'll see if he can help me

parts.words: Clearly, I'll see if he can help me
parts.note: a patient with poor eyesight hopes this specialist will let them see clearly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearly' and 'see' read as an expression of doubt, but literally mean clear sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who tests eyesight and supplies spectacles.

clue.text: Bug concealed originally in small picture

indicators.note: the first letter is placed in the word for a small picture

parts.note: an inset is a small picture within a larger one

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A listening device hidden within a little photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' suggests a listening device; it is a creepy-crawly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is an informal word for a small creeping creature.

clue.text: General talk or crack

definitions.meaning: the sharp bang of a gun firing

explanation.definitionFit: Both rumour that goes around and the loud bang of a gunshot.

clue.text: Madly desiring such a good seat

indicators.note: wildly rearranging the letters as if crazed

explanation.surface: Someone wildly covets a seat near the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' rearranges DESIRING; at a boxing match the best seats are close to the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats right beside a boxing ring give the closest view.
